free_tier.stated: 'USD 1 in free credits - enough to run your first deployment and explore the deploy loop', '30 days - your window to use the trial credit'. Quoted: 'Deployments run up to 24 hours each, and you can redeploy as many times as you like inside the 30-day window. GPUs up to the RTX 3090 are available. Anything above - including the RTX 4090, RTX 5090, and datacenter cards like the A100, H100, H200, and B200 - requires a non-trial account.' Prerequisites quoted: 'A valid email address (or Google / GitHub account). That's it! No credit card, no crypto wallet, no blockchain setup, no installation required.'

record.chaining: The permissionless path is the composable half: no KYC, no 30-day clock, funded in ACT, so it is the only decentralized lane here that a wallet alone opens with no identity check. It composes with any card-priced workload that cannot run locally.

identity_cost.detail: email, or a Google or GitHub account, and nothing else: the Quick Start prerequisites state 'A valid email address (or Google / GitHub account). That's it! No credit card, no crypto wallet, no blockchain setup, no installation required.', and a second Akash page states 'no card required'. No hold exists because no payment method is taken, so the debit and prepaid questions do not arise at signup; the paid permissionless route is funded in ACT and documents 'no KYC'.

an earlier announcement of the same free trial states 'USD 10 in credit'; the live Quick Start page states USD 1. The page is stale against the docs and the smaller number is the one the docs assert

third-party price index reports RTX 3090 on Akash at USD 0.150 per GPU-hour on-demand, one configuration, observed the same day
a second index lists RTX 3090 24Gi at USD 0.090 and an RTX 3060 12Gi at USD 0.080 from the Akash marketplace, giving the 0.09 to 0.15 range used in the division

evidence.quote: Deployments run up to 24 hours each, and you can redeploy as many times as you like inside the 30-day window. GPUs up to the RTX 3090 are available.

record.notes: The USD 1 trial credit is the current figure. An older blog post still advertises USD 10, so the trial was cut by 10x; a reader who finds the blog first will overestimate by 10x. The GPU price table at /pricing/gpus is client-rendered and returns empty rows, so individual rates below the RTX 3090 tier are not read off Akash's own page. Akash's own usage calculator computes the exact USD/GPU-hour. One inconsistency: Akash homepage marketing states H100s for USD 1.33 per hour while its own H100 pricing page states USD 2.73 as of 2026-10-20. The pricing page is the specific claim and the homepage line is undated, so the page wins. Egress does not bind at Akash: it documents zero egress fees, so the constraint here is the credit and the 24-hour deployment cap, not bandwidth.
